articles.title: Slap Row During Village Clash in Pilibhit district: Police Version Surfaces
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video from a village in Pilibhit district, Uttar Pradesh, has gone viral on social media, showing a heated altercation following a dispute allegedly over ₹350.

body.html:
A video from a village in Pilibhit district, Uttar Pradesh, has gone viral on social media, showing a heated altercation following a dispute allegedly over ₹350.

In the video, voices are heard arguing, with one person saying, “I gave you ₹350, why did you slap my brother?” The clip also contains abusive language. Allegations claim that after the dispute escalated, a group entered a house and assaulted members of the family. Around half a dozen people, including a woman, were reportedly injured and are undergoing treatment.

The viral video has also raised questions over a policeman allegedly slapping a young man during the incident. Social media users have criticised the alleged action, stating that if someone is guilty, legal procedures should be followed instead of physical assault.

However, the Pilibhit Police have issued a clarification. According to police, two groups were fighting among themselves when local officers intervened. During the intervention, some individuals allegedly pushed the police personnel.

Police said the entire incident is being investigated by the City Circle Officer, and necessary legal action will be taken based on the findings of the inquiry.

Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Love Triangle Ends in Brutal Murder: Actress Among 3 Arrested by Bagalagunte Police Station
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 40-year-old man was found murdered inside his rented house at Manjunath Nagar, under the limits of Bagalagunte police station in Bengaluru. Police have arrested three persons, including a woman identified as Bindu alias Urvashi, in connection with the crime.

body.html:
A 40-year-old man was found murdered inside his rented house at Manjunath Nagar, under the limits of Bagalagunte police station in Bengaluru. Police have arrested three persons, including a woman identified as Bindu alias Urvashi, in connection with the crime.

The deceased has been identified as Mohan Krishna Rao, a pigmy collector and small-time financier. The incident occurred on February 27, and the body was discovered after neighbours complained of a foul smell emanating from the house.

According to Deputy Commissioner of Police (North-West) D L Nagesh, a murder case was registered after inspection of the spot confirmed that Rao had been stabbed to death.

Investigation revealed that Bindu, who was in a live-in relationship with Rao, had developed a close relationship with Vinay, a lorry driver from the same locality. The two allegedly decided to marry, but Rao opposed their relationship and reportedly forced Bindu to stay with him.

Police said that on the night of February 18, the accused made Rao consume alcohol. They then allegedly tied his hands and legs, gagged him, stabbed him multiple times with a knife, assaulted him with an iron rod, and suffocated him using a plastic cover.

Dhanush Gowda, a friend of Vinay who was reportedly facing financial losses in his hotel business, was allegedly lured with money to assist in the murder.

After committing the crime, the trio fled. Police traced Bindu and Vinay to K.R. Nagar using call detail records, despite Bindu allegedly using multiple SIM cards. All three have been taken into custody and further investigation is underway.

Police stated that Rao and Bindu had rented the house two to three months ago, posing as a married couple. Both were earlier married and living separately from their respective spouses.

Bindu has claimed to have acted in a few Kannada films and to have worked as an associate director, but police said these claims are yet to be verified.

articles.title: Uncle Attacks PUC Student for Refusing to Quit Studies in Palya
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A second-year PU college student was allegedly assaulted by her uncle for refusing to drop out of school at Palya village in Nanjangud taluk of Mysuru district. The injured student has been identified as Poornima.

body.html:
A second-year PU college student was allegedly assaulted by her uncle for refusing to drop out of school at Palya village in Nanjangud taluk of Mysuru district.

The injured student has been identified as Poornima. According to the police complaint, the incident occurred after she returned home from writing her II PUC Kannada examination.

It is alleged that her uncle, Somanna, entered the house and attacked her with a stick, objecting to her continuing her education. Family members who intervened were also assaulted.

Poornima has alleged that she was being raised under Somanna’s care and that he did not want her to pursue her studies or build a better future.

She has been admitted to the Nanjangud Government Hospital and is undergoing treatment.

A case has been registered against Somanna and six others at the Nanjangud Rural Police Station. Police have launched an investigation.

articles.title: Bomb Threat Post Near Mosque Triggers Police Crackdown in Mangaluru
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The Ullal Police Station have registered a suo motu case after a provocative social media post threatened to explode a bomb near a mosque in the Ullal area of Dakshina Kannada district. A search operation has been launched to trace the person behind the post.

body.html:
The Ullal Police Station have registered a suo motu case after a provocative social media post threatened to explode a bomb near a mosque in the Ullal area of Dakshina Kannada district. A search operation has been launched to trace the person behind the post.

The threat was posted from an Instagram account named “Shankar11916”, which stated, “I will explode a bomb near a mosque in Ullal, please support me.” The comment quickly went viral, triggering public outrage.

Police sources said the post appeared on an Instagram page displaying the photograph of Suhas Shetty, identified as a Hindu organisation activist who was murdered earlier. Considering the sensitive nature of the matter, police acted swiftly to prevent any escalation.

Sudhir Reddy, Commissioner of Mangaluru City Police, has directed officials to immediately arrest the accused. Authorities have reiterated that strict action will be taken against those spreading religious hatred or fear through social media.

Police have urged the public to act responsibly online and refrain from sharing provocative content.

In recent months, several cases of inflammatory social media posts have surfaced in Mangaluru. The Cyber Crime Police recently arrested an individual for an objectionable post about Kadri Manjunatheshwara Temple. A few months earlier, the Commissioner had warned of invoking the Goonda Act against a group for posting Instagram reels with derogatory remarks targeting a specific community.

Given the sensitivity of Mangaluru city and Dakshina Kannada district, the Cyber Police are maintaining continuous surveillance through a dedicated Social Media Monitoring Cell. Strict action is being initiated under the IT Act and BNS against not only those who create such posts, but also those who like, share, or comment on provocative content.

articles.title: Tonsure Trip Turns Tragic: Speeding Scorpio Crushes Vendor, Sparks Road Blockade in Azamgarh
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A young cart vendor was killed after a speeding Scorpio rammed into him in Uttar Pradesh’s Azamgarh district, triggering protests by angry villagers. The incident occurred near Goga Saw intersection in the Jeyapur Kotwali area.

body.html:
A young cart vendor was killed after a speeding Scorpio rammed into him in Uttar Pradesh’s Azamgarh district, triggering protests by angry villagers.

The incident occurred near Goga Saw intersection in the Jeyapur Kotwali area. The deceased, identified as Harendra Sonkar, used to support his family by selling chickpeas from a cart. He died on the spot due to the impact.

According to police, the Scorpio driver was returning with his family from Maihar after attending a tonsure ceremony when the vehicle allegedly lost control and hit the cart. CCTV footage of the accident has also surfaced.

As news of the incident spread, family members and a large number of villagers reached the spot and blocked the road in protest. Police officials arrived and pacified the crowd after nearly an hour of persuasion and assurance of action.

The accused driver, Bharat Singh, a resident of Bhatauli Ibrahimpur village, has been detained. The Scorpio has been seized. A case has been registered based on a complaint, and further legal proceedings are underway.

#Azamgarh #UttarPradesh #RoadAccident #HitAndRun #CCTVFootage #PoliceAction #JusticeForHarendra #BreakingNews

articles.title: 3-Year-Old Girl, Driver Killed as Loader Overturns on Agra–Lucknow Expressway in Unnao
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A tragic road accident in the Bangarmau Kotwali area of Unnao claimed the lives of a three-year-old girl and a driver after a speeding loader overturned on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway on Tuesday morning.

body.html:
A tragic road accident in the Bangarmau Kotwali area of Unnao claimed the lives of a three-year-old girl and a driver after a speeding loader overturned on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway on Tuesday morning.

The accident occurred around 9 am near Gaharpurwa village when the loader, carrying 14 passengers, reportedly lost control after the driver allegedly dozed off. The vehicle struck a divider and overturned.

The victims were identified as Diksha (3), daughter of Monu, and the driver Murari, a resident of Makhi police station area. Both died on the spot.

According to Monu, a resident of Arsena village under Auras police station limits, he and several others from Gobra village had been working as labourers in Faridabad, Haryana, and were returning home for Holi in a rented loader when the accident occurred.

Upon receiving information, the UPDA rescue team and local police reached the spot and shifted the injured to a nearby health centre. After first aid, all injured were referred to the district hospital.

Inspector Akhileshchand Pandey confirmed that the injured were sent for treatment and the bodies were forwarded for post-mortem examination.

Those injured in the accident include Monu (27), his daughter Vaishnavi (8), his wife Bitto alias Pratibha (30), Rohit (24), Munshilal (50), Sonu (14), and Bhupendra (24), among others.

Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the accident, with preliminary findings indicating driver fatigue as a possible cause.

articles.title: Out-of-Control Car Crashes Into Parked Vehicle in Bilaspur; CCTV Captures Dramatic Spin
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A dramatic road accident was caught on CCTV in Bilaspur after a speeding car lost control and rammed into a vehicle parked outside a house. The incident took place in Dhenka village along the Bilaspur–Masturi road.

body.html:
A dramatic road accident was caught on CCTV in Bilaspur after a speeding car lost control and rammed into a vehicle parked outside a house.

The incident took place in Dhenka village along the Bilaspur–Masturi road. According to local sources, the car was travelling at high speed when it suddenly spun out of control in a film-like manner and crashed directly into a parked car on the roadside.

What CCTV Footage Reveals

CCTV footage shows the vehicle rotating abruptly before colliding with the parked car within seconds. The impact caused significant damage to the stationary vehicle.

At the time of the accident, a few pedestrians were passing nearby. They narrowly escaped injury as the car changed direction while spinning. A slight variation in its trajectory could have resulted in serious casualties.

Investigation Underway

No serious injuries were reported in the incident, though property damage was substantial. Sources indicate that the driver may have been a minor; however, officials are conducting a local inquiry to verify the driver’s identity and age.

Authorities are using CCTV footage to trace the vehicle and determine liability.

Police have reiterated that overspeeding and reckless driving in residential areas can have fatal consequences. Parents have been urged not to allow minors to operate vehicles, and drivers have been advised to strictly adhere to traffic regulations and speed limits.

articles.title: Army Jawan Alleges Assault by Police Inspector in Mathura; CCTV Clip Surfaces
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A controversy has erupted in Mathura after a soldier alleged that a police inspector assaulted him inside a house in the Jaint police station area. A CCTV video of the incident, which surfaced on Monday, reportedly shows the officer punching the soldier multiple times within seconds.

body.html:
A controversy has erupted in Mathura after a soldier alleged that a police inspector assaulted him inside a house in the Jaint police station area. A CCTV video of the incident, which surfaced on Monday, reportedly shows the officer punching the soldier multiple times within seconds.

The complainant, Radhacharan, a soldier in the Rajput Regiment, is currently posted in Bikaner and was home on leave. On Sunday around 11 am, he had gone to meet his friend Mahesh Kumar, who is posted with the 200th Battalion of the Border Security Force (BSF) in Manipur. Mahesh resides about 100 metres from Radhacharan’s house in Aajai Khurd village under Jaint police station limits.

According to Radhacharan, Aajai outpost in-charge Manoj Bhati arrived at the house with police personnel during a search operation linked to a Holi flag march and alleged wanted accused. He claimed that when police attempted to take Mahesh into custody over an old case, an argument broke out.

Radhacharan alleged that when he identified himself as an Indian Army soldier and objected to the alleged mistreatment, the inspector became aggressive and repeatedly punched him in the face. He further alleged that the police personnel also misbehaved with Mahesh’s elderly mother, Omvati Devi, and his wife.

Station in-charge Manoj Bhati, however, stated that the police were conducting a flag march and search operation in view of Holi and that Mahesh misbehaved when questioned about his brother.

CO Sadar Pitampal Singh said the matter is under investigation and that departmental action will be initiated if the officer is found guilty.

The soldier has submitted a complaint to the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), and further inquiry is underway.

articles.title: RPF Constable Saves Passenger from Slipping Under Moving Lichchavi Express at Prayagraj Junction
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman constable displayed exceptional courage and alertness at Prayagraj Junction, rescuing a passenger who slipped while attempting to board a departing train. The incident occurred at around 5:54 pm on platform number 6, just minutes before Train No.

body.html:
A woman constable displayed exceptional courage and alertness at Prayagraj Junction, rescuing a passenger who slipped while attempting to board a departing train.

The incident occurred at around 5:54 pm on platform number 6, just minutes before Train No. 14005 Lichchavi Express was scheduled to depart at 6:06 pm.

According to railway officials, Ashok Kumar, a resident of Kanpur, attempted to board the moving train in haste. During the attempt, his foot slipped and he fell into the dangerous gap between the platform and the train, putting his life at immediate risk.

Constable Geeta, who was on duty with the 16th Battalion of the Railway Protection Special Force (RPSF), noticed the incident and rushed towards the passenger. Acting swiftly, she pulled him out from between the train and the platform, preventing a potentially fatal accident.

The entire episode was captured on CCTV cameras installed at the platform.

Railway authorities have praised the constable’s prompt action and bravery. She will be awarded a commendation certificate under the “Operation Jeevan Raksha” initiative, which recognises railway personnel for life-saving acts.

Following the rescue, the train proceeded on its scheduled journey.

articles.title: Classroom Roof Collapses in Bharatpur School; Teacher’s Swift Action Saves 10 Students
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major tragedy was averted in Bharatpur district, Rajasthan after the roof of a classroom at a government school collapsed on Saturday afternoon (28 Feb 2026).

body.html:
A major tragedy was averted in Bharatpur district, Rajasthan after the roof of a classroom at a government school collapsed on Saturday afternoon (28 Feb 2026).

The incident occurred around 2:30 pm at Mahatma Gandhi English Medium Government School in the Nagla Bhagat area under Sewar police station limits. At the time, a teacher was explaining Holi celebrations to students when cracking sounds were heard from the roof.

According to school authorities, the beams began making sharp noises and visible cracks quickly widened across the ceiling. Sensing imminent danger, the teacher immediately evacuated all 10 students from the classroom.

Within approximately three minutes of the evacuation, the roof collapsed completely with a loud crash, filling the room with dust and debris. A video of the incident has surfaced, capturing the dramatic collapse of the roof along with its supporting beams.

Fortunately, all students were safely moved out in time, preventing what could have been a serious accident.

The school has a total strength of 28 students and functions from 10 am to 4 pm.

Headmaster Kavita Devi stated that the roof had not shown any visible signs of structural weakness prior to the incident. “The roof appeared normal. If it had been in a dilapidated condition, we would have informed the authorities earlier. The collapse happened suddenly. The matter is under investigation,” she said.

Authorities are expected to conduct a structural assessment to determine the exact cause of the collapse.
